questions.stem: In the dating of endometrium presence of secretory vacuoles beneath the nuclei of glandular epithelium denotes:
questions.solutionHtml:
Secretory phase
  • The presence of secretory vacuoles beneath the nuclei of glandular epithelium in the dating of endometrium denotes the Secretory phase.
  • During the secretory phase of the menstrual cycle, the endometrium undergoes changes in preparation for the potential implantation of a fertilized egg.
  • These changes are primarily driven by the hormone progesterone, which is secreted by the corpus luteum in the ovary after ovulation.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1007

questions.stem: The most favoured site of endometriosis is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ovary
  • The most favoured site of endometriosis is Ovary.
  • Endometriosis commonly affects the ovaries, and the presence of endometrial tissue outside the uterus can lead to the formation of cysts called endometriomas on the ovaries.
  • These cysts can cause pain, inflammation, and fertility issues.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1010

questions.stem: Endometriosis is defined by the presence of ectopic endometrial tissue at a site outside of the uterus, the word tissue denotes:
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • Endometriosis is characterized by the presence of ectopic endometrial tissue, which includes endometrial glands, endometrial stroma, and other components.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1010-12

questions.stem: Inactivation of which tumour suppressor gene is associated with endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial carcinoma:
questions.solutionHtml:
PTEN
  • Inactivation of the PTEN tumour suppressor gene is a common genetic alteration in both endometrial hyperplasias and endometrial carcinomas.
  • PTEN acts as a negative regulator of the PI3K/AKT signalling pathway, which is involved in cell growth, proliferation, and survival.
  • Loss of PTEN function leads to increased activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, promoting cell proliferation and survival and contributing to the development of endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1013

questions.stem: All of the following are true regarding type I endometrial carcinoma except:

options.label: B
options.text: Histological type is serous or clear cell

options.label: C
options.text: Most commonly mutated gene is PTEN

options.label: D
options.text: It has indolent nature and spread via lymphatics

questions.answerText: Histological type is serous or clear cell
questions.solutionHtml:
Histological type is serous or clear cell
  • The histological type of type I endometrial carcinoma is not a serous or clear cell. It is typically endometrioid carcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1015

questions.stem: Which of the following Option:s are true regarding type II endometrial carcinoma ? Serous or clear cell histology PTEN or KRAS mutation Low-grade tumour Arises in an atrophic endometrium Estrogen dependent Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1,4 correct
  • Type II Carcinoma generally occur in women who are about 10 years older than those with type I carcinomas,
  • Arise in the setting of endometrial atrophy.
  • Type II tumours are by definition poorly differentiated (grade 3) tumours and account for approximately 15% of cases of endometrial carcinoma.
  • Types: Serous or clear cell histology


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1015-17

questions.stem: The most common gene mutated in serous endometrial carcinoma is-
questions.solutionHtml:
TP53
  • Serous endometrial carcinoma is a high-grade type of endometrial carcinoma, and TP53 mutations are frequently observed in this subtype.
  • TP53 is a tumour suppressor gene that plays a crucial role in regulating cell cycle progression and DNA repair. Mutations in TP53 can lead to uncontrolled cell growth and tumour development.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1017

questions.stemHtml: A 58-year-old female presented with histologically proven endometrial hyperplasia 2 years back. At present, she has complaints of excessive bleeding PV and a CT scan shows a mass lesion in the uterus. The endometrial biopsy was taken and diagram of which is shown below. Based on histological features, Identify the type of tumour:
questions.solutionHtml:
Endometrioid carcinoma
  • The given clinical scenario with a histopathological image showing glandular growth patterns resembling normal endometrial epithelium is characteristic of endometrioid carcinoma.
  • It is typically composed of well-formed glands with variable degrees of cytological atypia and architectural complexity.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1016

questions.stemHtml: Endometrial biopsy of a 65-year-old female patient showing malignant epithelial and mesenchymal elements as shown in the diagram, based on the histological findings, identify the type of tumour.
questions.solutionHtml:
Malignant mixed müllerian tumor
  • The given clinical scenario with the histopathological image showing the presence of malignant epithelial and mesenchymal components is suggestive of a Malignant mixed müllerian tumour.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1018

questions.stem: Which of the following cytogenetic abnormality seen in leiomyoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • Leiomyomas are benign smooth muscle tumours that commonly occur in the uterus and are the most common tumours of the female genital tract.
  • These tumours have been shown to have cytogenetic abnormalities involving rearrangements of the high mobility group proteins HMGIC and HMGIY, as well as mutations in the MED12 gene.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1020

questions.stem: What is the most common site of metastasis in gestational choriocarcinoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lungs
  • The most common site of metastasis in gestational choriocarcinoma is the lungs.
  • Choriocarcinoma is a malignant tumour that arises from the trophoblastic cells of the placenta.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1019

questions.stemHtml: A 41-year-old female patient presented with excessive bleeding during the menstrual period and increased urinary frequency. After hysterectomy, the histopathology shown in the diagram, identify the lesion based on its characteristic findings.
questions.solutionHtml:
Leiomyoma
  • The given clinical scenario and a histopathological image showing bundles of smooth muscle cells with well-defined borders and minimal cytological atypia suggests the diagnosis of Leiomyoma


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1020
